key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implant performance depends on jointly designing implant geometry, biomaterial interfaces, and surface architecture for mechanical durability and bone integration.
engineering_relevance: Graded Ti–hydroxyapatite interfaces offer a plausible design strategy, but implant development must address gait-dependent stresses, micromotion, fatigue, and coating integrity.
method: Systematic review of implant concepts, biomaterials, and clinical translation.
Synthesis of geometry optimization, gait-phase finite element analysis, and osseointegration evidence.
Quantitative trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies.
evidence_signal: More than half of the empirical evidence remained at bench or simulation level, with animal and human/clinical studies providing a smaller validation layer.
watch_item: Evidence for graded Ti–hydroxyapatite architectures came predominantly from non-DWBI analog studies, so DWBI-specific durability and biological fixation remain unvalidated.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
